collection: Per V. Mortensen / Permo woven paper hearts
scope: Bounded preservation of original photo/template pairs and source evidence; no recursive site mirror. Paths under tmp await root-agent promotion to durable storage.

history.dateType: Date stated by source, not independently established first publication.
history.creditInterpretation: Mortensen explicitly distinguishes his drawings and variations from invention of woven hearts and their earlier patterns. Do not label him inventor or original designer of every motif.
history.earlierSources: The source refers generally to ladies’ magazines 25–35 years earlier; no titles, issues or earlier designers are identified.
history.rightsEvidence: Neither the inspected Permo heart/template pages nor Hunodan listing grants reuse or redistribution permission. Permo’s copyright reminder concerns linked Bramming nisse art, not a license for the heart designs.
history.archiveVersionCheck: A successful bounded CDX prefix query through 2009 returned 37 JPEG URLs: 32 combined-template designs and five hjerte photos. It reported no changed payload digests within that period; the initial internal-wildcard query returned empty and is not used as evidence.
history.familyIndexComparison: The retrieved 2001 and 2009 heart index pages both list the same 32 designs across seven populated families. The 2009 circles and figurines pages reference the same five image filenames as their 2001 captures.
history.missingSection: Cut Out Patterns remains labelled in progress in both index pages; fetching its 2009 link hjsil-01.htm returned404. This does not establish that no copy exists elsewhere.
history.pdfFinding: The retrieved template pages link combined JPEG drawings and photographs. No cutting-template PDF appeared in the bounded171-media-URL archive inventory.

helpfulLeads: Any saved original Permo site backup or later direct contact with the creator could clarify missing cut-out patterns and permissions.
Old ladies’ magazine titles/issues or pattern sheets matching these 32 motifs could identify the earlier designers whom Mortensen explicitly distinguishes from himself.
An independent backup destination would make preservation durable without consuming more of the user’s local disk.
